title: Cross-Layer Intrusion Detection in 5G O-RAN: Gains and Limits of Fusing Radio Telemetry with Network Flow Records
authors: Fard H.; Komarov I.; Wunder G.
venue: IEEE International Conference on Cyber Security and Resilience (CSR), Lisbon
testbed: uses the UCD corpus (no new testbed)
attack_types: as per corpus; DoS emphasised in the confusion analysis
feature_modalities: DU radio telemetry (1 s aggregation across all UEs active in the DU, cumulative byte counters first-differenced to per-second rates, remaining KPIs as mean and sd per window -> 44 features) and CU Zeek flow records (conn.log, http.log, files.log; per-window sum/mean/sd with log transform on skewed features -> 68-72 features). Sliding windows W in {5,10} s, stride 2 s
model: seven architectures: Logistic Regression, XGBoost, Random Forest, GRU, Temporal Convolutional Network, Transformer, Residual MLP. Hyperparameters tuned on one seed at W=10 then FROZEN across all evaluations
baseline_models: single-modality variants of the same architectures
split_strategy: run-disjoint over 42 runs; all windows from a run go to exactly one partition; ~70/15/15 by run count, stratified by attack family with at least one run per family per partition; ten seeds giving 19-26 train / 7-12 val / 8-12 test runs
false_alert_evaluation: partial - reports a 1% FPR operating point, but no alert volume and no base-rate sweep
limitations: DoS-to-Benign confusion of 27-46% (mean ~37%) persists across all 42 tested configurations and is near-identical for network (37.6%), radio (37.5%) and fusion (37.3%) on XGBoost, which the authors attribute to windowed statistical aggregation rather than model capacity. Stacked fusion is UNSTABLE at this sample size: ROC-AUC sd +/-0.171 to 0.182 for TCN and Transformer, which they attribute to leakage sensitivity at 42 runs. They state NetsLab-5GORAN-IDD is the only public O-RAN corpus with paired CU flow records and DU radio telemetry, and that confirming transfer beyond this testbed needs new paired captures from independent deployments
relevance: CRITICAL - nearest prior work on our D_A; sets the in-distribution reference and constrains our novelty
what_our_project_learns: (i) run-disjoint splitting on this corpus is the established protocol, so a random split would be indefensible; (ii) radio beats flow IN-DISTRIBUTION by 8.5-11.7 ROC-AUC points (radio 0.925-0.961 vs network 0.827-0.851) - the first half of our H4 sign-flip is now prior work with numbers attached; (iii) DECISIVE FOR OUR D-008: they align the two modalities by RUN-RELATIVE timestamps from the RAW per-category archives, not the published summary CSV, and for DoS traces lacking telemetry timestamps they assign time from the sample index at 1 Hz. This is an existence proof that our route (a) works, and it supplies the method; (iv) they had only 42 runs and report fusion instability (ROC-AUC sd up to 0.182) at that size, so our own small-sample warning is corroborated by prior work; (v) their authors explicitly name cross-testbed transfer as the open question - which is exactly our RQ1
potential_gap: fusion gains measured in-distribution only. Cross-deployment transfer, tail latency, resource cost, alert burden, calibration and robustness are all absent, and the authors name cross-testbed transfer as the stated open question. The second half of our H4 (radio features HURT transfer) is untested by anyone
verification_status: GOOD: arXiv full text (HTML) read 2026-09-20. Method, splits, feature counts, headline numbers and limitations all extracted from the paper

authors: Obiuwevwi L.; Rechowicz K. J.; Jayarathna S.; Bouk S. H.; Afrin F.; Barati C. N.; Moghim N.; Nanou V.; Rahman M. E.; Shetty S.
ric_type: FlexRIC (real Near-RT RIC, model embedded in the xApp)
attack_types: none - network-state classification, not intrusion detection
feature_modalities: cross-layer RAN state: MAC, RLC, PDCP, GTP, UE count
model: logistic regression and shallow MLP exported as deterministic C inference modules, no external ML runtime
baseline_models: the two models compared against each other
latency_evaluation: yes - inference-only 1-5 us (LR) and 10-25 us (MLP); end-to-end below 4 ms; CDF characterisation plus a noise ablation

title: Performance Analysis of an AI-Based IDS xApp for Cyberattack Anomaly Detection in O-RAN Near-RT RIC
venue: ScienceDirect (Tech Science Press host), article S152614922600202X
dataset: NetsLab-5GORAN-IDD (O-CU network layer plus O-DU radio telemetry)
ric_type: deployed in a Near-RT RIC environment (claimed)
feature_modalities: O-CU network layer and O-DU radio telemetry
model: LSTM, CNN, Transformer, Autoencoder. In-distribution F1: CNN 0.9974, Transformer 0.9966, LSTM 0.9949, Autoencoder 0.9644. A structurally optimised LSTM is selected on the performance/efficiency balance
latency_evaluation: yes - peak inference ~600 ms (LSTM, CNN) and ~850 ms (Autoencoder); LSTM, CNN and Autoencoder all stay within 1000 ms at the maximum load of 80,000 instances on both datasets
p99_latency: YES - approximately 140 ms at p99 for the selected LSTM. This CONTRADICTS the EXP-000 gap claim that no retrieved O-RAN IDS study reports p99. Note 140 ms is 14x a 10 ms budget and 0.14x a 1000 ms budget, so the same measurement passes or fails depending only on which end of the O-RAN near-RT range is chosen
external_validation: no - but they do compare O-CU against O-DU as two datasets and report the Autoencoder degrading between them (F1 0.9644 -> 0.9115, precision 0.9688 -> 0.8477). That is a cross-LAYER comparison within one deployment, not cross-deployment transfer
limitations: assumes a 1000 ms near-RT budget, the permissive end of the 10 ms - 1 s range; F1 94.87% (O-CU) and 99.49% (O-DU) are in-distribution only
relevance: HIGH - a second latency comparator on the same corpus, reaching the OPPOSITE deployability verdict to P04 purely by choosing a different budget
what_our_project_learns: I11 is now quantified rather than argued. Their selected LSTM has p99 ~140 ms. Against B = 1000 ms it passes comfortably; against our B = 10 ms it fails by 14x. One measurement, two opposite verdicts, decided entirely by which end of the O-RAN 10 ms - 1 s range the author picks. Sweeping B and reporting the crossing point is therefore not a hedge, it is the only way to make the verdict a measurement
potential_gap: single budget value at the permissive end; no cross-deployment evaluation; no CPU/RAM; no alert burden at a realistic base rate; in-distribution F1 above 0.99 with no transfer test is exactly the reporting pattern our paper critiques
verification_status: MODERATE: publisher still returns HTTP 403; fields come from two independent detailed search-result snippets (2026-09-20) that agree. Numbers are usable for internal reasoning but the PDF MUST be obtained before any of them is cited in the manuscript. Author list still NOT VERIFIED
